sections.name: Hook
lines: t_hook
You tap your phone hundreds of times a day. But it isn't feeling your touch. It's feeling your electricity.
t_title
Here's what happens in that split second, in five steps.

sections.name: The invisible grid
lines: t_grid
Step one. Under the glass is a grid of see-through wires. Rows running one way, columns the other.
t_layers
They're made of a metal oxide so thin you can see right through it, sandwiched between the glass and the display.
t_field
Where they cross, the screen holds a tiny electric field. Hundreds of little sensors, all waiting.

sections.name: Your finger steals charge
lines: t_finger
Step two. Your body conducts electricity. So when your finger gets close, it pulls a little of that field away.
t_drop
The change is tiny, but the screen is built to notice it.
t_glove
That's why gloves don't work, and a pencil won't either. Touchscreen gloves have metal thread sewn into the fingertips.

sections.name: Scanning the grid
lines: t_scan
Step three. A controller chip checks every crossing, row by row, many times every second.
t_speed
A full scan takes just a few thousandths of a second, so it keeps up even when you scroll fast.
t_locate
It finds the spots with the biggest change, and works out the centre. That's where you touched, to within about a millimetre.

sections.name: Many fingers
lines: t_multi
Step four. Every crossing is measured on its own, so the screen can track several fingers at once.
t_palm
It can even ignore your palm resting on the glass, by the size and shape of the touch.
t_gesture
Software watches how those points move. Two fingers spreading apart? Pinch to zoom. One sliding fast? That's a swipe.

sections.name: Why it glitches
lines: t_water
Step five. Water conducts too. So raindrops on your screen can look like fingers, and cause ghost touches.
t_old
Older screens worked differently. Two flexible layers had to be pressed together, which is why you used to push so hard.

sections.name: Recap
lines: w_recap
A hidden grid. Your finger steals a little charge. A chip scans every crossing, tracks every finger, and turns it into a tap.
outro
So every tap is a tiny electrical event. Follow for more of the tech you use every day.
